lies.speaker: Silas
lies.said: Umar is dead, a Civilian. I walked my round last night and saw nothing useful, only lamps and empty lanes. I won't hang anyone on noise. Pia, you're out on the water at odd hours. Where were you when the bell went?

lies.speaker: Hugo
lies.said: Umar's death is a loss, and I want facts, not fear. My night: I marked copybooks by lamplight until midnight, alone, and heard nothing. Pia, your alibi is nets and fog with no witness, and so is mine, so neither of us can be measured by it yet. Let's test each account against what the Dawn bell told us, not against mood. Pia, did you see anyone on the quay?

lies.speaker: Silas
lies.said: Pia, I walked the quay at the second bell. Your lamp was dark, your nets on the steps, and nobody else on the stones. Elsie, you count echoes like a clerk. Who gains if a name goes up fast? Answer plainly: what did you see after dark?

lies.speaker: Silas
lies.said: Elsie, I passed the quay at the second bell. Pia's lamp was dark, her nets on the steps, and no one else on the stones. You keep asking me the hour, yet from your shelves you saw no one at all. Tess, your window looks onto the square. What did you see after dark?

lies.speaker: Silas
lies.said: Tess, no. My lantern never paused under your window. I keep to the quay and the lanes, and I see what moves there. Elsie, you have asked me the hour three times and given none of your own. Your shelves saw nothing, you say. Convenient, for a clerk who wants a name. Answer me before you ask me again.
